notes: Adds small unquoted-brace helpers on Token and uses them for every brace check in the dispenser and parser, including import/snippet handling, blockTokens and the address parser, and removes the now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive(). Tests are thorough, covering parsing, dispenser behavior, nested blocks, snippets, backtick quotes and the unquoted-error case, though brace checks in other packages such as httpcaddyfile were not audited.

The fix adds small `isOpenCurlyBrace`/`isCloseCurlyBrace` helpers that ignore quoted tokens and uses them consistently at every brace check in the dispenser and parser (addresses, directives, imports, snippets, `blockTokens`), and drops the now-redundant `wasQuoted` check; the dispenser and parser tests cover quoted `{` and `}`, backticks, nested blocks, snippets and an unquoted-brace error case.

Correctly applies --once after config consolidation through a focused DeriveSingleRunScenario helper that keeps exec/env/tags/options, rejects multiple scenarios and the vus/iterations/duration/stage flags, and works across run, cloud run and archive; tests are thorough at both unit and command level, and the only minor gaps are that equivalent env-var shortcuts are silently discarded rather than rejected and the single-element map loop reads slightly oddly.

Applies the --once transformation right after config consolidation. It keeps exec, env, tags and scenario options, creates a single shared-iterations 1/1 scenario, rejects multiple scenarios and the CLI shortcut flags, and reaches run, cloud run and archive through optionFlagSet. Minor gaps: env-var shortcuts (K6_VUS, K6_ITERATIONS) are silently discarded rather than rejected, and a CLI-specific error message lives in lib/executor. Tests are thorough, covering the unit, run, archive and cloud paths.

This fixes the reported bug: it stops collapsing imports by ConfigResource and returns every block as a slice, so all for_each and count instance imports in the root module are honored. The weakness is the override heuristic. It compares only the resource key and ignores module instance keys. When either key is dynamic, the parent block overrides every child block for that resource, so child for_each imports for other instances are silently dropped, the same class of silent loss the issue complains about. That gap likely explains the failing hidden test, and the tests are otherwise solid.

Fixes the reported bug by returning a slice instead of a map keyed by ConfigResource, so all root-module for_each/count import blocks survive, but the new parent-overrides-child heuristic drops every child import for a resource whenever either side's key is dynamic (for_each imports), and it ignores module instance keys, silently reintroducing the same kind of drop the issue reports (likely the failing hidden test).

Fixes the root cause by wrapping a parenthesised `*NumberLiteral` in a Wrapped unary-plus `*DurationExpr`. It updates the zero-division, zero-modulo and must-be-positive checks to see through the wrapper via a recursive helper, and adjusts `Pretty` to match `String`. The synthetic node changes the AST for cases like `offset (5)` from a static offset to an expression offset, and `((5m))` still collapses to `(5m)`. Tests are thorough: printer, parse-error, prettier and promqltest evaluation.

Fixes the root cause by wrapping a parenthesised `*NumberLiteral` in a synthetic unary-ADD `*DurationExpr` with `Wrapped` set, only when experimental duration expressions are enabled. It keeps the existing parse-time checks working through the wrapper (`durationLiteralValue` for positive-duration, division-by-zero and modulo-by-zero), and it fixes `Pretty()` so it drops the unary `+` the same way `String()` does. The synthetic ADD node is a mild representational workaround and error ranges exclude the parens, but it is consistent with the existing code and backed by thorough round-trip, AST, error, prettier and engine tests.

The patch adds a recursive ancestor-slug resolver and a `Dir` override in `TargetPathDescriptor`, which correctly rewrites URLs for slugged sections, taxonomies, terms and their descendants, including non-section subdirs and nested sections. Pages with no slug anywhere keep the existing path logic. Weak spots: `parent.PathInfo()` would panic if `Parent()` ever returned nil, and slugs are ignored when permalink config is used, but the test covers the main scenarios well.

The patch adds a `Dir` override to `TargetPathDescriptor` and computes it by walking the section ancestors and applying any slug, so slugs on sections, taxonomies and terms reach every descendant (nested sections, leaf bundles, non-section subdirs, taxonomy and term). It falls back to the existing paths when no slug is found and respects `disablePathToLower`; the main drawbacks are recomputing the ancestor walk for every page and a new public descriptor field. The added test is thorough, covering default-language passthrough, nested unicode slugs, non-section subdirs, leaf bundles and taxonomy/term slugs.

The design follows the issue: a `ReturnError` sentinel is turned into a panic in `evalCall` and caught per template by `walkReturnable`. It also scopes returns correctly for `template`/`block` and `try`, keeps `return add 1 2` working through a rewrite, and updates the fork script so the patch survives re-forking. Weaknesses: it still needs static `HasReturn` detection in partials; it silently changes bare `return` from returning an empty string to returning the output rendered so far (or nil); it changes the `Executer` interface signature; and it rewrites an existing test's expected error. One hidden test and the package suite fail.

A sound sentinel-error design that removes the old contextWrapper and AST rewrite, traps `ReturnError` per template invocation, re-panics through `try`, keeps `return add 1 2` working and updates the fork script; but one hidden test fails, the semantics of a bare `{{ return }}` and of returning inside `block`/`define` are a debatable design choice, and an existing test's expected error message was changed to fit the new behavior.
